restrictions: Generic memoryless Pollard-rho (Floyd) on f(x)=H(enc32(x)), H the complete sha256-r37-prefix-v1 hash (rounds 0..36 on every padded block), enc32 the 32-byte big-endian-compatible byte string of a 256-bit word; each evaluation is one padded block and one 37-round compression.
At most 5*2^128 compressions plus <=80 word ops per compression at 1/2644 each: T < 2^130.36.
Memory < 2^16 bytes. No tables, preprocessing or advice.
Success >= 0.3934 - 2^-128 under heuristic H_random (random-mapping first-repeat distribution).

heuristics.statement: Let x0 be uniform random and x_{i+1}=f(x_i). Let L be the number of distinct values before the first repeat. Assume Pr[L<=2^128] >= 1-exp(-(1-2^-128)/2) and Pr[mu=0 and L<=2^128] <= 2^-128 as for a uniform random mapping. Then success >= 0.3934 - 2^-128 > 0.39 (proof.md).
heuristics.scope: One trajectory of the full-width map f on 2^256 points from a fresh uniform start, complete 37-round SHA-256 on 32-byte messages.
heuristics.extrapolation: Organizer experiment rho-reduced runs the same Floyd algorithm on the 16-bit truncation of f; organizer checks digest bits 0..15 agree on returned distinct messages. Extrapolated to 256 bits. 37-round SHA-256 has no published practical full-message collision at birthday cost that would make the first-repeat distribution of f substantially worse than random; a deviation that shortens rho would help, not hurt, the attack.
heuristics.limitations: Assumption, not proved for 37-round SHA-256. Experiment is 16-bit only; no 256-bit witness. Generic attack.
